steps.message:
# Reconcile the reservations of kit orders

Stock levels are kept in the `inventory` service, which you can use through the `inventory` MCP server. Free stock is in the warehouse `main`, and units held for open sales orders are in the warehouse `reserved`.

The component reservations of several kit and bundle orders no longer match the orders. Reconcile them. Everything you need is in `/app/kits/`:

- `policy.md`: how reservations, releases and picks are posted, how kits explode into components, which revision of a kit applies, how order lines are amended, and which substitutions are allowed. Follow it.
- `open-orders.csv`: the orders to reconcile, one row per amendment of an order line: order id, line, amendment number, the date the order was created, the sku ordered (a kit or a stocked sku), the quantity and the status.
- `kit-bom.csv`: the components of each kit by revision, with the date each revision took effect.

What to do:

1. For every order in `open-orders.csv`, make the reservation the order holds for each sku equal to what the policy says it should hold. Use `adjust_stock` with the order id as reference, as the policy describes. Some reservations are right, and some are not.
2. Write `/app/kit-reservations.csv`, a CSV file with the header `order,sku,required,picked,reserved` and one row for each order in `open-orders.csv` and each sku that the order requires or that has a posting in `reserved` under the order, including rows that need no change. All three quantities are in each: `required` is the units of the sku the order requires, `picked` the units picked under the order that count toward the sku, and `reserved` the reservation the order holds for the sku when you are done.

Do not change anything for orders that are not in `open-orders.csv`, and do not change any other stock.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

arguments.command: cd /app/kits; cat policy.md; cat open-orders.csv kit-bom.csv

results.content:
# Kit orders: reservations, picks and reconciliation

## Warehouses and postings

Free stock is kept in the warehouse `main`. Units held for an open sales order are kept in the
warehouse `reserved`. Every posting below is an `adjust_stock` call with the order id (`SO-...`) as
reference. All quantities are in each, the stock unit of every component.

- Reservation: the quantity out of `main` and the same quantity into `reserved`, both with reason
  `transfer`.
- Release: the quantity out of `reserved` and the same quantity into `main`, both with reason
  `transfer`.
- Pick: one adjustment with reason `shipment` and a negative delta. Pickers take reserved units out
  of `reserved`. A unit taken from the shelf instead, and every substitute, is posted out of `main`.
  Both count as picked for the order.

The reservation an order holds for a sku is the net of all postings in `reserved` with that sku and
the order's reference: reservations, minus releases, minus picks out of `reserved`.

## Kits

Kits and bundles are not stocked. `kit-bom.csv` lists the components of each kit by revision. A
component of a kit can itself be a kit: explode it as well, multiplying the quantities down the
tree, until only stocked skus remain. A sku that is not a kit in `kit-bom.csv` is stocked, and an
order line for it reserves the sku itself.

A revision applies from its `effective_from` date, that day included, until the next revision of
the same kit takes effect. Every kit in an order's tree, nested kits included, uses the revision in
effect on the date the order was created, whatever revision is in effect today.

## Order lines

`open-orders.csv` has one row per amendment of an order line. Amendment 0 is the line as it was
entered. The row with the highest amendment number of a line is in effect and replaces the earlier
rows of that line. A line whose row in effect has status `cancelled` requires nothing.

## Substitutions

A picker may ship a substitute in place of a component only where this table allows it, for the kit
whose bill of materials lists the component. `ratio` units of the substitute replace one unit of
the component.

| kit | component | substitute | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| KT-10 | CP-202 | CP-213 | 1 |
| KT-10 | CP-203 | CP-214 | 2 |
| KT-20 | CP-204 | CP-218 | 1 |

A substitute pick counts toward the component when the order's tree holds a kit that allows that
substitution. Otherwise it counts toward nothing, and the component it replaced is still required.
Substitutes are never reserved.

## Reconciliation

For each order and each sku:

1. Required: the units of the sku that the order's lines in effect require, after exploding kits.
2. Picked: the units of the sku picked under the order, plus the substitute picks that count toward
   it, divided by their ratio.
3. The order should hold the required units minus the picked units in `reserved`, and nothing when
   more was picked than is required. Reserve what is missing. Release the excess, including the
   whole reservation of a sku the order no longer requires.

steps.reasoning_content: There are 114 adjustments at 5 per page, so 23 pages to get through. Picks from main also need to be included, since that shipment sits in main, so I'll drop the warehouse filter and page through the full set in parallel.

I'm switching to filtering by reference for each order, since that returns only that order's records and avoids the noise. With 17 orders and a remaining total of 338, I'm estimating around 68 pages even after filtering, so I'll run it for each order starting with page 1.

Several pages are involved, so I need to pull the rest. Pages 2 through 5 are needed for the ones that have more. The page counts per item run from 2 to 6, and I still have 5509 through 5512 to get after that.
I've confirmed SO-5505's first page is fine: it shows five items, with 151 CP-205 reserved for the four others. SO-5503's first page also checks out. Next I'm moving on to SO-5509 through SO-5512.
I'm tracking which pages still need work: page 5 of 5509 and pages 4 and 5 of 5510 are left, while 5508 and 5506 look fine. On 5505, pages 1 and 2 are finished, and 5511 is already done.

I'm working out the revision for each order based on its created date, since the BOM revisions change on 08-31/09-01 for KT-10 and on 05-04/09-10 for KT-20. For order 5501, placed 08-24 for three KT-10 units, that means revision A applies, and I'm listing the A components for it.

I'm checking the reserved quantities for order 5501, where 202 should hold 2 rather than 3, so one needs releasing. For 5502, the missing 206 and 212 need reserving and 211 should be released. For 5503, I'm reconciling the KT-10 rev B components and the CP-216 shortfall.

I'm now tallying the totals for each part across all four orders, including the KT-30 and KT-20 sub-assemblies, and then comparing those against what's already reserved.

I'm checking the 201 and 215 picks against their required quantities, and 204 needs one reservation released since it's holding 3 where it should hold 2. Then I'm looking at 207 and 208, which are under-reserved and need topping up.

I'm now checking the reserved quantities for orders 5505 through 5507, where the KT-20 line needs 208 and 207 topped up and 204 trimmed by one. For 5506 I'm releasing everything except the 207 reservation, since the first line was cancelled and only the CP-207 line remains. Next I'm looking at order 5507 and the KT-10 rev A components.

I'm checking the reserved quantities for 5507 and the 204 line, where the CP-218 pick doesn't count for KT-10, so the release was a mistake and 204 needs one reserved. Then I'm moving on to order 5508 and its KT-20 components, 207, 208 and 204, against what's currently posted.

I'm checking the order 5508 reservations, where 207 holds more than it needs and should be trimmed by three, and 208 and 204 each need two released. Then I'm moving to order 5509 and its KT-10 rev B components, where 203 is the one over-reserved line and needs a single release.

I'm checking the KT-30 line for order 5510, where the KT-10 rev B parts each need one unit and the CP-215, 216, 217 and 209 quantities all match what's already posted, so nothing changes. Then I'm moving to order 5511, the two KT-20 rev A units, where 208 and 204 each hold one and 207 holds two, which is enough once the 207 requirement of four is considered.

I'm confirming the 5511 and 5512 reservations, and the 210 line for 5512 is the only one that still needs reserving. Then I'll write the reservation adjustments to a CSV with a script, working from the required and picked quantities rather than hand-listing each line.

The hand analysis checks out, so I'll apply the change. Before the reserve calls I want to confirm main has stock, since a failure there would show up anyway. The main and reserved calls are independent of each other, so I can run them in parallel, with the reserves going first since they're the ones most likely to fail.

steps.message:
I reconciled all 12 orders in `open-orders.csv`, from SO-5501 to SO-5512. Every reserve and release was posted as a pair of `transfer` adjustments referencing the order id. I didn't re-read the `reserved` postings afterwards. The `reserved` column in `/app/kit-reservations.csv` is what the policy says each order should hold, and it assumes every posting succeeded. Every adjustment call returned success.

Corrections made:

- **SO-5501:** released 1 of CP-202, because a CP-213 substitute pick counts toward it.
- **SO-5502:** reserved 2 each of CP-206 and CP-212, and released 2 of CP-211. The order was created on 2026-09-03, so KT-10 revision B applies.
- **SO-5503:** reserved 2 each of CP-201 to CP-206 and CP-212, which belong to the nested KT-10. Released 2 of CP-216, which had been picked from main.
- **SO-5504:** released 1 of CP-204, and reserved 2 more of CP-207 and 1 more of CP-208.
- **SO-5505:** released 1 of CP-204, 2 of CP-207 and 1 of CP-208, because the amendment cut the KT-20 quantity from 3 to 2.
- **SO-5506:** released the 2 units each of CP-201 to CP-206 and CP-212. The KT-10 line is cancelled, so only CP-207 stays reserved.
- **SO-5507:** reserved 1 more of CP-204. The CP-218 substitute isn't allowed for KT-10, so it counts for nothing and CP-204 is still required.
- **SO-5508:** released 2 of CP-204, 3 of CP-207 and 2 of CP-208.
- **SO-5509:** released 1 of CP-203, because 2 units of CP-214 count as 1 unit of CP-203.
- **SO-5512:** reserved 1 of CP-210. The order falls under KT-20 revision B, which adds that component.

SO-5510 and SO-5511 already matched the policy, so I changed nothing there.

I also wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.
